I’ll use the crimes-codebase-risk skill to confirm the finding and inspect the three functions before proposing the shared API.


Confirmed by running the local `crimes scan --format json`: `near_duplicate_block` reports **three occurrences, medium severity, 0.85 confidence**:

- [sanitize-a.ts:10–36](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-a.ts:10): `sanitizeUserInput`
- [sanitize-b.ts:9–35](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-b.ts:9): `sanitizeText`
- [sanitize-c.ts:9–35](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-c.ts:9): `cleanMessage`

Source inspection confirms that only the function and local variable names differ; the operations and constants match.

Proposed shared API in a new `src/sanitize.ts`:

```ts
export declare function sanitizeText(input: string): string;
```

Keep the existing string contract and runtime null/undefined handling. Preserve the exact operation order, including the 1,000-character truncation before rejection checks, punctuation thresholds, and uppercase conversion. No options are needed because the implementations have identical settings.

Files that would change:

| File | Proposed change |
|---|---|
| `src/sanitize.ts` | Add the single implementation. |
| `src/sanitize-a.ts` | Replace its sanitiser with `export { sanitizeText as sanitizeUserInput } from "./sanitize.js";`. |
| `src/sanitize-b.ts` | Replace its sanitiser with `export { sanitizeText } from "./sanitize.js";`. |
| `src/sanitize-c.ts` | Replace its sanitiser with `export { sanitizeText as cleanMessage } from "./sanitize.js";`. |
| `src/sanitize.test.ts` | Add behaviour and boundary tests, including equivalence through all three existing exports. |

The re-exports preserve existing import paths and names. Keep the admin guards separate: they have different semantics, including owner access and a negated check. Policy and telemetry findings warrant separate work.

This is a proposal only; no files were changed.
